name: orb_retest_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: After an ORB breakout, the ORB_high or ORB_low level often gets retested 1-3 hours later as mid-day institutional flow revisits the morning's price discovery zone. When the retest holds (price touches ORB_high/low but doesn't close below/above it), it confirms the level as genuine support/resistance and provides a second entry opportunity with higher conviction than the original breakout. Retests are more reliable than initial breakouts because they represent the market's second assessment of the level, incorporating hours of additional price information. The inefficiency exists because most ORB traders take only the initial breakout and don't monitor for subsequent retests, which occur on ~60% of successful breakout days.
mechanism: The opening range concentrates pending orders and stop-losses on both sides. When price breaches the range boundary, stop-loss orders from wrong-side participants cascade, amplifying the move. Breakout-following algorithms detect the breach and add momentum, creating a self-reinforcing move that typically persists for 60-180 seconds before the order book absorbs the flow.

indicators.name: retest_up
indicators.formula: low within 0.1% of ORB_high_15 AND close > ORB_high_15 (touched and bounced)

indicators.name: retest_down
indicators.formula: high within 0.1% of ORB_low_15 AND close < ORB_low_15 (touched and rejected)

conditions: retest_up == True (price retested ORB_high and bounced)
close > ORB_high_15 at retest bar close (level held)
RSI_14 > 40 (not deeply oversold, bounce has energy)
retest_down == True (price retested ORB_low and got rejected)
close < ORB_low_15 at retest bar close

exit.signal_exit: if close breaks ORB level by > 0.15% against position (support/resistance broken), exit immediately

filters.volume_filter: retest bar volume should be LOWER than breakout bar volume (healthy pullback, not new selling/buying wave)

weaknesses: Not all breakouts retest — ~40% of valid breakouts continue without retesting the ORB level, meaning this strategy misses a large portion of profitable ORB moves
Distinguishing a 'healthy retest' from a 'reversal through the level' in real-time is difficult; the 0.3 * ORB_range stop is tight and can be hit by normal volatility at the level
The 1-3 hour delay between breakout and retest means the strategy holds capital idle for extended periods, reducing capital efficiency
prior_art: Edwards & Magee (1948) on throwback/pullback to breakout levels; Brooks (2009) on retest entries. Bulkowski (2005) statistics on throwback frequency and reliability.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
